experiment.domain: probabilistic calibration and reproducible tabular classification
experiment.research_question: When does post-hoc temperature scaling improve held-out probabilistic calibration on a small public tabular classification dataset, and how stable are its gains across repeated calibration and test splits?
experiment.hypothesis: On the fixed WDBC dataset and logistic baseline, fitting one positive temperature on a separate calibration split will reduce held-out Brier score and ECE on average across 30 repeated stratified splits while preserving ranking; log-loss behavior and the shared-bin ECE outcome will be reported with a separate bootstrap uncertainty estimate.
experiment.method: Use the official UCI WDBC CSV (569 rows, 30 predictors). For 30 fixed seeds, split each class into 60% training, 20% calibration, and 20% held-out test rows. Standardize from training rows only, fit L2-regularized logistic regression on training rows, fit temperature by calibration-set log loss, and report raw versus scaled probabilities only on untouched test rows. Report the shared raw-probability-bin 10-bin ECE as the like-for-like headline, retain the per-score 10-bin ECE as a binning sensitivity, recalculate all aggregates with an independent standard-library validator.

parameters.calibration_method: positive scalar temperature fitted on calibration log loss

experiment.stopping_rule: Execute exactly 30 fixed splits; do not inspect interim values or extend the run based on observed effects.

limitations: The study uses one public diagnostic dataset, one logistic model family, and one temperature-scaling implementation.
Thirty repeated splits describe finite-sample stability; they do not establish a universal calibration guarantee or compare every calibration method.
The WDBC features are diagnostic measurements, so this analysis does not evaluate clinical deployment or decision utility.
The percentile endpoints summarize variation across the prespecified splits and are descriptive ranges rather than inferential confidence intervals.

reviewers.focus: Audit the replication question, literature-facing interpretation, hypothesis, external-validity limits, and whether every statement stays within the WDBC study.
Audit split isolation, calibration leakage, optimization, metrics, exact replay, independent recalculation, and numerical traceability.

Search aggressively for generic AI prose, inflated novelty, unsupported certainty, citation-shaped filler, suspiciously symmetrical claims, and hidden negative or mixed results; require concrete evidence.
